traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.35, 0.3, 0.26], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 235): 'stout spreading branches forming a broad compact round-topped or conic head'.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): "ranging from 16 to 100 feet tall (5-30 m)"; "The largest trees are up to 150 feet (45 m) tall".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): "Leaves range from 2 to 6 inches (5-15 cm) long".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): "sclerophyllous evergreen leaves".

traits.leaf_life_years.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): "Leaves remain on trees for about 3 years".

traits.leaf_margin.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): leaves "lanceolate to oblong and have entire margins".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives a width.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): on the H. J. Andrews Experimental Forest (western Oregon Cascades), flowering "from mid-June to mid-July" over 3 years; rangewide April into July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): on the H. J. Andrews Experimental Forest "its fruit ripened from mid-August to early September"; fruits take 2 growing seasons.

generator.params.note: Oregon white oak's values, changed by hand for golden chinquapin: a straight trunk with a cone-shaped crown of stout branches at right angles to the bole (FEIS, Meyer 2012), so a stronger leader, wide branch angles and no fork. path_half fitted so the tree grows to its reference height. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius.

allometry.note: USDA Forest Service Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005, public domain): its fitted age-to-dbh and dbh-to-height equations for coast live oak (Quercus agrifolia) in the Sacramento Valley region (Sacramento, CA; 60 open-grown park and street trees aged 2.4-134.5 years), since it has no chinquapins: the database's evergreen tree of the chinquapin's family in California, from the city whose valley oaks stand for Oregon white oak, evaluated: 18.2 m and 80 cm at 50 years; 20.6 m and 98 cm at 80 years. Was 18 m and 45 cm at 80 years, rough sizes within FEIS's ranges (Meyer 2012).

appearance.note: By eye, after FEIS's description (Meyer 2012): dark green lanceolate leaves with entire margins and golden undersides (the accent); cream catkins; the spiny 4-valved bur drawn as a husked nut, the nearest card to a bur. Bark thick and furrowed.

generator.params.leaf_years.note: FEIS's giant chinquapin review (Meyer 2012, read 2026-10-15): "Leaves remain on trees for about 3 years".
